messages:
alex: Heads up — after upgrading the JS SDK to v2.4 the sample app sometimes hangs on long pagination loops. Repro steps: run sampleapp/paginator with 10k items, concurrency=8, windowSize=256 and it will freeze after a few minutes.

maria: Ugh. Any error logs or stack traces?

alex: No thrown exception, it just stops producing requests. App still alive, CPU low. I captured the thread dump and the SDK logs:
```
2026-11-02T16:12:01.234Z DEBUG sdk: acquiring window-semaphore
2026-11-02T16:12:01.235Z DEBUG sdk: token refresh triggered (401)
2026-11-02T16:12:01.237Z DEBUG auth: start-refresh
2026-11-02T16:12:03.900Z DEBUG auth: refresh-complete, new-token
2026-11-02T16:12:03.901Z DEBUG sdk: waiting on window-semaphore (held by another request)
// then nothing for minutes
```

alex: The semaphore wait never times out. Looks like a deadlock between the token refresh path and the windowing lock.

sam: Which SDK? Node or browser?

alex: Node (js-sdk 2.4.0). Python sample app (py-sdk 1.x) doesn't hang — it queues retries differently.

maria: Do you have the snippet of how sampleapp is calling the paginator? Could be client-side backpressure + auth retry blocking each other.

alex: Yep:
```
const p = new Paginator({concurrency: 8, windowSize: 256});
for await (const page of p.listAll(items)) {
  await processPage(page);
}
```
we rely on Paginator internally to manage the in-flight window.

jordan: Sounds like when a request hits 401 the SDK does a sync `await refreshToken()` while still holding the window semaphore. If another inflight request also hits auth it waits for semaphore to be released -> deadlock when refresh path tries to acquire same semaphore to re-enqueue/flush.

eli: I remember a parity note in the backlog: Node SDK used to `await` refresh inline while Python deferred refresh to an async queue. That could explain differences.

alex: Took a quick patch: changed refresh to `backgroundRefresh()` (non-blocking) and added a `semaphore.tryAcquire(timeout=2000)` fallback. With that the freeze goes away in my run. But want a proper fix.

maria: Good quick mitigation. Can you open a small repro branch in sampleapps and link it? Also include a minimal test that simulates simultaneous 401s under high concurrency.

ci-bot: CI started for branch alex/sdk-auth-windowing-repro #42

sam: Long-term we should avoid holding window locks during network auth operations. Two options: 1) move auth refresh outside of the window critical section, or 2) make refresh idempotent and single-flight without touching window. Prefer #2: single-flight token refresh that other requests await but doesn't block window bookkeeping.

jordan: Agree. Also add a watchdog to window semaphore: if held > X ms, log stack and force release (dangerous but useful for debugging).

eli: For SDK parity: update node docs to match py behavior and add the single-flight refresh util to both SDKs. Add a regression test in devex/e2e for pagination+auth storms.

alex: I'll draft the PR: change refresh to single-flight, remove blocking acquire inside refresh path, and add an optional semaphore timeout (off by default). Will include repro branch and CI test.

maria: Thanks. Please tag me and sam in the PR. Also add a note in the changelog about potential hangs for apps on v2.4.0 so customers can pin or patch. :warning:

alex: Will do. Thx all.

ci-bot: CI passed for branch alex/sdk-auth-windowing-repro #42 (tests: 14/14) :white_check_mark:
